description: This topic explores Kingdom Monera (prokaryotic bacteria and cyanobacteria) and Kingdom Protoctista (mostly unicellular eukaryotes), covering their cell structure, movement, feeding, reproduction, and economic and medical importance.

mcq.questionText: Which feature is found in members of Kingdom Monera?

options.text: A true nucleus enclosed by a membrane
A large cell with many nuclei

mcq.explanation: Members of Kingdom Monera are prokaryotes, meaning their cells have no true membrane-bound nucleus; their genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm.

mcq.questionText: Bacteria that are rod-shaped are called:
mcq.explanation: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria. Cocci are spherical, spirilla are spiral, and vibrio are comma-shaped.

mcq.questionText: Which bacterial shape is described as spherical or round?
mcq.explanation: Cocci (singular: coccus) are round or spherical bacteria.

mcq.questionText: What is the main method of reproduction in bacteria?

options.text: Budding of new organisms from leaves

mcq.explanation: Bacteria mainly reproduce asexually by binary fission, where one cell divides into two identical cells.

mcq.questionText: Cyanobacteria are also commonly known as:
mcq.explanation: Cyanobacteria are called blue-green algae because they are prokaryotes that contain chlorophyll and can carry out photosynthesis.

mcq.questionText: Which structure protects and gives shape to a bacterial cell?
mcq.explanation: The rigid cell wall surrounds the bacterial cell, giving it shape and protection.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following organisms belongs to Kingdom Protoctista?
mcq.explanation: Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryote placed in Kingdom Protoctista. Bacteria are in Monera, mushrooms in Fungi, and maize in Plantae.
Amoeba uses pseudopodia (false feet) made by flowing cytoplasm both to move and to surround and capture food.

mcq.questionText: Which protoctist moves by means of many tiny hair-like structures called cilia?
mcq.explanation: Paramecium is covered with many cilia that beat in a coordinated way to move it through water.

mcq.questionText: Euglena is unusual because it can:

options.text: Only make food by photosynthesis and never feed
Make its own food in light and also feed when light is absent
Live only inside the human stomach

mcq.explanation: Euglena has chloroplasts and photosynthesises in light, but in darkness it can also feed on ready-made food, so it shows both plant-like and animal-like features.

mcq.questionText: The protoctist that causes malaria in humans is:
mcq.explanation: Plasmodium is a parasitic protoctist that causes malaria and is spread by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

mcq.questionText: Which one is a beneficial role of bacteria in the soil?

options.text: Fixing nitrogen to improve soil fertility

mcq.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria change nitrogen gas into compounds plants can use, increasing soil fertility.

mcq.questionText: Bacteria are used in the dairy industry mainly to:

options.text: Make yoghurt and cheese from milk

mcq.explanation: Useful bacteria such as Lactobacillus ferment milk to produce yoghurt and cheese.

mcq.questionText: Which feature is NOT found in a typical bacterial cell?
mcq.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes and lack a membrane-bound nucleus, although they do have a cell wall, cell membrane and cytoplasm.

mcq.questionText: Spirogyra is best described as a:

options.text: Filamentous green alga in Kingdom Protoctista

mcq.explanation: Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga with spiral chloroplasts and is classified in Kingdom Protoctista.

fib.questionText: Organisms whose cells have no true nucleus are described as _____.
fib.explanation: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus; all members of Kingdom Monera are prokaryotes.
Vibrio are curved, comma-shaped bacteria; the cholera-causing bacterium is an example.

fib.questionText: Bacteria reproduce asexually by a process called _____.
fib.explanation: In binary fission, a bacterial cell copies its genetic material and splits into two identical cells.

fib.questionText: Blue-green algae that can carry out photosynthesis are also called _____.
fib.explanation: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes of Kingdom Monera, also known as blue-green algae.

fib.questionText: The false feet that Amoeba uses for movement and feeding are called _____.
fib.explanation: Pseudopodia are temporary extensions of cytoplasm used by Amoeba to move and to engulf food.

fib.questionText: Paramecium moves through water using tiny hair-like structures called _____.
fib.explanation: Cilia are short hair-like structures that beat together to move Paramecium and sweep food towards it.

fib.questionText: Euglena swims by lashing a long whip-like structure called a _____.
fib.explanation: Euglena moves using a single flagellum, a long whip-like thread that lashes the water.

fib.questionText: The disease caused by Plasmodium and spread by mosquitoes is called _____.
fib.explanation: Plasmodium causes malaria, which is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito.

fib.questionText: Bacteria that change nitrogen gas into compounds usable by plants are called _____ bacteria.
fib.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert nitrogen gas into nitrogen compounds, improving soil fertility.

fib.questionText: Most members of Kingdom Protoctista are unicellular and have a true nucleus, so they are described as _____.
fib.explanation: Protoctists are eukaryotes because their cells contain a true membrane-bound nucleus.

tf.questionText: All members of Kingdom Monera are prokaryotic organisms.
tf.explanation: Kingdom Monera contains only prokaryotes, such as bacteria and cyanobacteria.

tf.questionText: Bacteria contain a true membrane-bound nucleus.
tf.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes and do not have a true membrane-bound nucleus.
Spirilla are spiral or coiled bacteria.

tf.questionText: Cyanobacteria cannot make their own food.
tf.explanation: Cyanobacteria contain chlorophyll and make their own food by photosynthesis.
Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryote classified in Kingdom Protoctista.
Paramecium moves using cilia, not pseudopodia; pseudopodia are used by Amoeba.

tf.questionText: All bacteria are harmful and cause diseases.
tf.explanation: Many bacteria are useful, for example in nitrogen fixation, decomposition, making yoghurt, and producing antibiotics.

tf.questionText: Plasmodium is a protoctist that causes malaria in humans.
tf.explanation: Plasmodium is a parasitic protoctist responsible for malaria.

tf.questionText: Some bacteria help in decomposition, returning nutrients to the soil.
tf.explanation: Decomposer bacteria break down dead organisms and waste, recycling nutrients into the soil.

tf.questionText: Spirogyra is a flowering plant that produces seeds.
tf.explanation: Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga in Kingdom Protoctista; it does not produce flowers or seeds.

summary.questionText: State two main characteristics of Kingdom Monera.
summary.correctAnswer: Members are prokaryotic (no true nucleus) and are usually unicellular microscopic organisms.
summary.explanation: Monerans such as bacteria and cyanobacteria are single-celled prokaryotes lacking a membrane-bound nucleus.

summary.questionText: List the four main shapes of bacteria.
summary.explanation: Bacteria are grouped by shape into cocci, bacilli, spirilla and vibrio.

summary.questionText: Name three parts found in a bacterial cell.
summary.correctAnswer: Cell wall, cell membrane and cytoplasm (also genetic material and sometimes a flagellum or capsule).
summary.explanation: A bacterial cell has a protective cell wall, a cell membrane, cytoplasm and free genetic material, plus extra structures in some species.

summary.questionText: Briefly describe how bacteria reproduce by binary fission.
summary.correctAnswer: The cell copies its genetic material and then splits into two identical daughter cells.
summary.explanation: Binary fission is asexual reproduction where one parent cell divides into two genetically identical cells.

summary.questionText: Give two beneficial uses of bacteria to humans.
summary.correctAnswer: Making yoghurt and cheese, and producing antibiotics; they also fix nitrogen and decompose waste.
summary.explanation: Useful bacteria are used in food production, medicine, soil fertility and recycling of nutrients.

summary.questionText: Give two harmful effects of bacteria.
summary.correctAnswer: They cause diseases such as cholera and tuberculosis, and they spoil stored food.
summary.explanation: Harmful bacteria cause infectious diseases in humans and animals and lead to food spoilage.

summary.questionText: State two characteristics of Kingdom Protoctista.
summary.correctAnswer: They are eukaryotic (have a true nucleus) and are mostly unicellular organisms living in moist or watery places.
summary.explanation: Protoctists are eukaryotes, usually single-celled, and commonly found in water or damp habitats.

summary.questionText: Compare how Amoeba, Paramecium and Euglena move.
summary.correctAnswer: Amoeba uses pseudopodia, Paramecium uses cilia, and Euglena uses a flagellum.
summary.explanation: Different protoctists use different structures for movement: false feet, cilia, or a whip-like flagellum.

summary.questionText: Explain why Euglena is said to have both plant-like and animal-like features.
summary.correctAnswer: It has chloroplasts and photosynthesises like a plant, but it can also feed on ready-made food and move like an animal.
summary.explanation: Euglena shows a mix of features, making it hard to classify simply as a plant or an animal.

summary.questionText: Describe the medical importance of Plasmodium.
summary.correctAnswer: Plasmodium is a parasite that causes malaria, a serious disease spread by the female Anopheles mosquito.
summary.explanation: Malaria caused by Plasmodium is a major health problem, especially in tropical regions like Tanzania.

hoq.questionText: A farmer notices that maize grown after a season of beans is healthier and greener, even without adding much fertiliser. Which process by bacteria best explains this observation?

options.text: Bacteria spoiled the beans and released poison
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the bean roots enriched the soil with nitrogen compounds
Bacteria caused a disease that killed weeds only
Bacteria removed all water from the soil

hoq.explanation: Legumes such as beans have nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules that add nitrogen compounds to the soil, improving fertility for the next crop.

hoq.questionText: A student observes a microscopic organism in pond water that has chloroplasts, swims using a single whip-like thread, and seems to move towards light. To which organism and kingdom does it most likely belong?

options.text: A coccus bacterium in Kingdom Monera

hoq.explanation: Chloroplasts, a single flagellum and movement towards light are typical of Euglena, a eukaryotic protoctist. Plasmodium is also a protoctist (not a moneran), and bacteria are prokaryotes.

hoq.questionText: In a village, many children fall sick with fever after the rainy season when mosquitoes increase. A health worker links the illness to a single-celled parasite in the blood. Which control measure would most directly reduce this disease?

options.text: Using mosquito nets and clearing stagnant water to stop mosquito breeding
Adding more nitrogen-fixing bacteria to the soil
Eating more yoghurt made by bacteria

hoq.explanation: The parasite is Plasmodium, which causes malaria spread by mosquitoes. Using nets and removing stagnant water reduces mosquito breeding and bites, directly lowering malaria transmission.
